thread:
maria.k: Seeing a cluster-wide IOPS spike on a subset of GPU nodes, also getting dmesg nvme errors on node gpu-pool-34 :eyes:
raj.s: Copy of alerts: nvme_io_ops > 450k for 00:03, disk_latency_ms p95 1200ms, some mariadb pods started OOMing (weird)
infra-bot: [ALERT] nvme.smart.failed on gpu-pool-34 (smartctl: 1 prefail attribute) — https://dash/reports/176543
lee_ops: I pulled iostat and top during the spike, looks like the ephemeral-cleaner job spawned 24 rm -rf workers and they hammered /local/nvme/ephemeral. iostat:

---- iostat sample ----
Device:         r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await svctm  %util
nvme0n1       30000 420000 1200000 16800000   40.0    30.2  1.10  0.75  98.2
-----------------------

maria.k: ugh, %util 98 is nasty. Are those rm jobs expected?
raj.s: The cleaner is supposed to batch deletes via xargs -P4, not spawn 24. Looks like a recent change in cleanup-worker (PR #412) increased concurrency.
julia_p: Reverting that PR now. Will push a hotfix to constrict to -P4 and add a rate limiter.
sre-oncall: Recommend cordoning gpu-pool-34 and moving running jobs. No more scheduling until we confirm disk health.
lee_ops: Agree. Also SMART shows growing reallocated sectors on nvme0n1. Not yet catastrophic but correlated with IO storm + unlink churn.
maria.k: Impact on model-serving? Latencies spiked ~3-4x for some endpoints, GPUs were idle waiting on IO. Could cascade to cost if we keep retrying.
raj.s: For immediate mitigation: 1) cordon + drain noncritical pods: `kubectl drain gpu-pool-34 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60` 2) restart nvme-cleaner service on nodes that are healthy: `systemctl restart nvme-ephemeral-cleaner` 3) run fsck in maintenance window if SMART fails
lee_ops: I started the drain for two nodes (gpu-pool-34-a,b). Jobs moved fine. Putting a temporary TFO/annotation to avoid new batch cleaners: `kubectl annotate nodes gpu-pool-34-* infra/cleanup-disabled=true`
julia_p: Hotfix deployed to cleanup-worker image tag hotfix/limit-concurrency. Rolling update to staging then prod - rolling concurrency from 24 -> 4.
infra-bot: Deploy started: cleanup-worker -> hotfix/limit-concurrency (8 nodes at a time).
sre-oncall: Please schedule a maintenance window tomorrow 02:00 UTC to run full nvme health checks and consider replacing nvme0n1 on gpu-pool-34 if reallocated sectors > 1000.
maria.k: Also need follow-up: audit other clusters for similar change drift (why did PR get merged without load test?) and add CI e2e that simulates high unlink rates.
raj.s: I'll file the postmortem and assign owners. Quick note: cost spike due to retries estimated ~$1.2k for the hour — we should bill to incident.
lee_ops: For record, attached logs snippet and the failing dmesg lines: `nvme nvme0: Completed Command: STATUS: media error` — pushing to ops-runbook.
maria.k: Thanks everyone. Keep the thread updated. :thumbsup:
